title: uml4termux device-run evidence record
description: One JSON file per verification run, produced on an Android/Termux device by `bin/uml4termux evidence` (or written by hand). Device runs are the ONLY place a UML boot is ever proven: GitHub-hosted runners cannot execute the arm64 UML port. Evidence files are validated by .github/workflows/device-evidence.yml and by `make evidence-check` / `ci/local-ci.sh`. Fields marked required are the minimum needed to make the claim auditable: what device, which kernel, which capabilities were probed, and the verdict. Anything a reviewer would have to take on faith (a screenshot, a raw log, a kernel release string) belongs in the optional fields -- cite it, do not assert it.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written against. Bump when a required field changes.

project_version.description: uml4termux VERSION at the time of the run (contents of the VERSION file).

run_id.description: Stable identifier for this run: a git commit SHA, a CI run id, or a device-local timestamp id.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with timezone offset, when the record was written.

device.description: The physical device the run happened on. Without this the evidence cannot be reproduced or compared.

model.description: Device model, as reported by getprop ro.product.model.

android_release.description: Android release, as reported by getprop ro.build.version.release.

abi.description: Primary ABI of the userspace running UML.

unprivileged.description: Must be true. uml4termux is only supported unprivileged: if root was involved the result does not describe the supported configuration.

termux_version.description: Termux app version and package source (F-Droid/Play/GitHub), when known.

cpu_count.description: Number of online CPUs visible to the Termux process.

host.description: Userspace environment the UML process ran in.

kernel.description: The guest kernel that was booted (not the Android host kernel).

booted.description: true only if the guest reached userspace (init ran) during this run.

arch.description: SUBARCH the UML build targeted. Any value other than um/arm64 does not describe this project.

release.description: Guest uname -r string, when the guest booted. Required in practice if booted is true; left optional so a failed boot can still be recorded.

source_commit.description: Downstream port commit (zalexdev/Raymer8639 port) the kernel was built from.

boot_seconds.description: Wall-clock seconds from process start to the guest reaching userspace.

capabilities.description: Which of the project's headline capabilities were actually exercised and observed in this run. Each entry is a boolean probe result plus, ideally, the observation that backs it.

vcpu_count.description: Number of guest vCPUs configured for the run.

observed.description: Free-form observations: exact versions, commands, and one-line results quoted verbatim from the run. This is where a reviewer looks for the 'how do you know' behind each capability.

host_port_check.description: Command whose success is the port-forwarding proof, e.g. a curl against 127.0.0.1:$host_port.

known_limits_observed.description: Limits from the project's own documentation that showed up (or did not) in this run, recorded rather than hidden.
examples: no 32-bit compat (i386 binaries do not run)
phantom processes possible after guest exit

verdict.description: Overall result of the run. 'pass' asserts every capability set to true in this record was directly observed; 'partial' is the honest label when something was assumed, flaky, or only partly exercised.

notes.description: Anything a reader must know to reproduce or to distrust this record.

artifacts.description: Pointers to bulky evidence (raw console log, screenshots). Raw logs must match .gitignore (*.raw.log) and are usually attached to the CI run rather than committed.

probe.description: A single capability probe: did it work, and what backs that claim.

evidence.description: One line of verbatim output, or a command, that justifies 'ok'.
